body: This PR updates calibration pipeline to use ClimaCalibrate v0.7. Some changes include using the diagonal term machinery for the covariance matrix and removing Distributed as a dependency.
title: Update calibration pipeline to use ClimaCalibrate v0.7

body:
<!--- THESE LINES ARE COMMENTED -->
## Purpose 
This PR corrects a few subtleties in the gravity-wave modules:
1. The drag is now correctly distributed over stretched and deep-atmosphere grids via a mass-weighted scaling.
2. With a shallow model top, the non-orographic gravity-wave (NOGW) scheme no longer deposits all the momentum at the top-most cell. Instead, the momentum is spread over three cells in a single column, and a minimum of three cells on the sphere.
3. In the bottom and top cells, $N^2$ was computed with about half the gradient $dT/dz$, and this is now corrected with one-sided differencing.


## Content
The summary below is generated by Claude Code and reviewed by me (Ray):

1. **Non-orographic drag conserves momentum on any grid.** The wave kernel now returns the flux each layer loses, and this flux is turned into a drag by dividing by the mean mass of the two cells on either side of the layer, `m = ρJ/ΔA`, with `ΔA` the area of the column's bottom face. Cell centres sit midway between faces, so half of each cell's mass lies inside the layer. The column-integrated momentum tendency `Σ m X` then equals the deposited flux exactly, and the escaped flux at the model top is likewise divided by the damping layer's mass `M_R` directly. This fix conserves momentum on uniform, stretched and deep-atmosphere grids. Before this fix, the kernel divided by an estimate of the layer's mass, `√(ρ_k ρ_{k+1}) Δz`. This led to an error of about 0.3% on a uniform grid and about 1.6% on a deep-atmosphere grid.
2. **The non-orographic damping layer spans at least the top three cells** (`NOGW_MIN_DAMP_CELLS`). This layer receives the momentum flux that escapes through the model top. With a model top below `nogw_damp_pressure` (for example the 30 km top and 85 Pa that many configs use), the pressure rule picked only the top cell, and all the escaped flux went into one cell. A warning is logged when the damping level is expanded to fit the minimum three cells. Single columns always use the top three cells.
3. **Buoyancy frequency in the bottom and top cells (non-orographic and orographic).** `ᶠinterp` copies the end-cell temperature onto the boundary face. This gave about half of `dT/dz` in the end cells, so `N²` was about 10% off. The end cells now use the gradient across the face to their only neighbouring cell. Interior cells are unchanged. For OGW, this logic is now in a new non-allocating helper, `ogw_temperature_gradient!`.

The reference counter is bumped, as the three fixes to the gravity-wave drag schemes above change the output of every CI run with gravity-wave drag.

### Also in this PR
- **The NOGW drag is limited by its magnitude, not per component.** The drag vector is scaled to at most 3e-3·√2 m/s², as in OGW (`limit_gravity_wave_forcing!`), so it keeps its direction where the limit kicks in. Non-finite values are still set to zero, and a `@debug` check reports them.
- **A warning when `dt_nogw` or `dt_ogw` is not a whole number of model steps.** The warning fires in `aquaplanet_equil_allsky_gw_raw` (1800 s intervals with a 400 s step), so it will show in that job's log.
- **`set_beres_launch_state!`.** The Beres launch-level search is moved, unchanged, into its own function. This is so that the Beres single-column test computes its launch state from its own profiles instead of reading values left over from the startup callback.

### Some additional points
- **`NOGW_MIN_DAMP_CELLS = 3` is set as a module constant, not a ClimaParams parameter.** This is because it is a numerical safety floor, not physics to tune. The closest precedent is the `RAW_TOPO_ARTIFACT_*` constants in `orographic_gravity_wave.jl`.
- **The thin-damping-layer warning fires once per run.** The check reduces over all columns and MPI ranks, so it runs only at the first call; the global flag `NOGW_DAMP_LAYER_CHECKED` is reset when the NOGW cache is built. The three-cell minimum damping layer is applied on every call.
- **The mass is divided out after the wave kernel, not inside it.** The `waveforcing` kernel is close to the 4 KiB GPU kernel-parameter limit and is shared by AD99 and Beres, so the kernel returns the flux and the cell masses are applied to its output instead of inside the kernel. The kernel still uses ρ and z for the breaking test and the density scale height.
- **Flux convention.** The launched flux is computed as per unit area of the _column's bottom face_. An alternative would be per unit area at the launch height, which would differ by about 0.3% on a deep-atmosphere grid (on a shallow grid the two are the same).

## Tests
- `test_ad99_momentum_budget.jl`: the column budget must equal 1 to `rtol = 1e-10` on uniform, stretched, shallow-sphere and deep-sphere, and Earth-topography sphere (with terrain-following `J` and `ΔA`) grids. Before, the target was `cosh(Δz/2H)` (to `rtol = 1e-4`), plus a check that the ratio is within 0.01 of 1.
- `test_beres_sphere_integration.jl`: the launch level in every column is set by `nogw_source_pressure`, and the damping level is set by `nogw_damp_pressure` with the three-cell minimum. For a 45 km model top, the thin-damping-layer warning is activated, and `N` is checked in both end cells to match the one-sided formula.
- `test_beres_single_column.jl`: Two checks: (1) in column mode, `compute_tendency!` puts the damping layer in the top three cells, and (2) the Beres launch state is the first level at or above `gw_ztop`.
- `test_ogw_blocked_drag.jl`: on a single column, with even and stretched spacing and a curved temperature profile, `ogw_temperature_gradient!` must match the intended formula in every cell to `rtol = 1e-10`:
  - inside the column, the difference across the cell's two faces;
  - in the bottom and top cells, the one-sided difference to the only neighbour.

  The profile is chosen so that reading the wrong face or using the wrong spacing also fails, not only the old half-gradient value.
- `test/callbacks.jl`: `warn_if_not_whole_steps`.
- `test_ad99_momentum_budget.jl` also checks that the magnitude limit keeps the drag's direction and that building the NOGW cache resets the damping-layer check.
- `test_nogw_mima.jl`: now runs on MiMA's own heights with a uniform source amplitude (`Bt_n = Bt_s = 0`), and has a numeric check. Each month, the zonal-mean drag must match MiMA's with a pattern correlation of at least 0.95 for `u` and 0.55 for `v`, and an RMS ratio for `u` between 0.55 and 0.8. The ratio is below 1 because of the momentum-conserving rule for the escaped flux: it is about 1.0 between 100 and 1 hPa and 0.66 in the three damping cells.

Moving the division out of the kernel does not change the drag. On one model state with a sheared wind, the old and the new code give the same drag in every cell, up to Float32 rounding.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)
- NOGW and OGW implement the same end-cell `dT/dz` rule separately. They could share one helper.
- The column-integral weight `J / (J/Δz)_bottom` is written out in three places: ClimaCore's `column_integral_definite!`, `microphysics_cache.jl`, and here. A shared helper would remove the repetition.

body: This PR pins ClimaCore to v1.0.8 in the GitHub CI test job. With v1.0.9, released today, `correct_implicit_advection_tendency!` allocates 96 bytes under `--check-bounds=yes`, which `Pkg.test` turns on, so GHA CI fails on every branch ([`zs/plume-turb-entr`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl/actions/runs/45464612410), [`as/precip-energy`](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl/actions/runs/45448923700), #5007). Runs on v1.0.8 pass. The package compat and the Buildkite environment are unchanged.
title: Fix ClimaCore to 1.0.8

body:
Adds an optional term to the `InvZEntrainment` velocity-scaling prefactor that raises dynamical entrainment where a draft is moister than its environment:

`(c_sub / H) max(0, RHʲ - RH⁰ʲ)^p_sub`

where `H` is the pressure scale height and both relative humidities are taken against saturation over the draft condensate, so supercooled draft liquid mixed with air at ice saturation counts as subsaturated. For a saturated draft, the factor is the deficit `1 - RH⁰ʲ`; it vanishes in overcast layers and is small below cloud base.

- Off by default (`entr_subsat_coeff = 0`; `entr_subsat_power = 2`). Both are provisional parameters, validated when the parameters are built.
- Documented in `prophet_closures.md` and `NEWS.md`; unit tests in `test/parameter_tests.jl`.
title: Add optional subsaturation entrainment to InvZEntrainment
